assessment.title: Status Assessment
assessment.footer: Your answers are private and secure
assessment.footerCritical: Critical risk: any answer other than Never sets status to high risk immediately.

questions.q1: Does your partner expect you to be available 24/7 and demand detailed explanations if you don't answer immediately?
questions.q2: Do you feel your partner is trying to isolate you from friends or family?
questions.q3: Do you feel like you are 'walking on eggshells' to avoid an explosion or anger from your partner?
questions.q4: Does your partner restrict your access to money or demand an account of every small expense?
questions.q5: Does your partner define extreme jealousy or possessiveness as an expression of love?
questions.q6: Does your partner tend to belittle you, insult you, or make you feel worthless?
questions.q7: Do you feel like you always become the 'guilty one' in every argument, even when it's not true?
questions.q8: Are there topics you avoid bringing up because of fear of a violent or extreme reaction?
questions.q9: Does your partner dismiss your feelings or claim you are 'too sensitive' when you express pain?
questions.q10: Do you feel like you have no one to turn to and must hide the reality of your relationship from others?
questions.critical1: Has there been an increase in the frequency or severity of violence recently?
questions.critical2: Has your partner ever threatened to kill you, themselves, or others if you leave?
questions.critical3: Has your partner ever tried to choke you, or do they have access to a weapon?

safetyTips.title: Safety Tips
safetyTips.tip1: Trust your intuition: If something feels off, it usually is.
safetyTips.tip2: Digital Privacy: Use incognito mode for sensitive searches.
safetyTips.tip3: Emergency Code: Set a 'safe word' with your trusted contact.
safetyTips.tip4: Location Safety: Keep your GPS off when it's not strictly necessary.
safetyTips.tip5: Early Pattern Identification: Pay attention to repetitive argument patterns. If you're only "pleasing" to keep the peace, it's a warning sign.
safetyTips.tip6: Discreet Consultation: Consulting a social worker or counselor is for gaining tools and maintaining safety, not just for ending a relationship.
safetyTips.tip7: Emotional Documentation: Use the hidden diary to document your feelings, not just events. It helps track if the situation is improving or worsening.
